plain: Download a copy of a remote repository, including its full history, into a new folder.
when: You want to work on a project that already exists on GitHub.

plain: Show what changed, what is staged, and which branch you're on.
when: Before every commit. It's the 'where am I?' command of Git.

plain: Stage every change in the current folder for the next commit.
when: You've finished a chunk of work and want to include all of it in one commit.

plain: Save the staged changes as a commit with a short message.
when: You've staged the right files and want a checkpoint you can return to.

plain: Upload your commits to the remote named origin and remember main as the upstream branch.
when: Your commit is ready to share, or you're publishing a new local repo for the first time.

flags.meaning: set the upstream branch for future pushes
force push only if nobody else pushed

plain: Fetch remote changes and replay your local commits on top of them, keeping history linear.
when: The remote moved ahead and you want to avoid a noisy merge commit.

flags.meaning: replay your commits instead of merging

plain: Create a new branch and switch to it in one step.
when: You're starting a feature or fix and don't want to commit straight to main.

flags.meaning: switch back to the previous branch

plain: Show a compact, visual history of every branch as an ASCII graph.
when: You need to understand how branches diverged or where a commit went.

plain: Show line-by-line changes that are not staged yet.
when: Before staging, to check exactly what you're about to commit.

plain: Park your uncommitted changes so you can switch branches with a clean working tree.
when: You need to pull or switch branches but aren't ready to commit. Restore with git stash pop.

flags.meaning: restore the latest stash and remove it

plain: Throw away the last commit and every uncommitted change, moving the branch back one step.
when: Almost never. If you only want to undo a commit, use git revert instead — it keeps history.

flags.meaning: move the branch but keep changes staged

plain: Create a new commit that undoes an earlier commit, without rewriting history.
when: You need to undo something that's already pushed and shared.
